newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso ends up due to higher rates.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends up due to higher rates.

text.p: * Central Bank follows trend with lower dollar bid rate
The Philippine peso closed sharply higher on Monday at 26.236 to the dollar from 26.252, induced by the higher overnight interest rates, traders said.

"The market started with a firm peso because of the high overnight rate," said a local bank dealer. Banks had to sell their dollars to ease their peso liquidity after their dollar-buying spree last Friday.
The day's average yielded 26.241 from 26.257 on Friday.
Market volume fell to $133.50 million from $187.80 million.
The average rate in the overnight money market rose to 11.96875 from 11.09375. Similarly, the benchmark 92-day bill rate increased to 11.593 from 11.536 percent during the regular Monday auction.
Traders said the higher domestic interest rates triggered the inflow of interest arbitrage money from foreign investors, leading to a stronger peso.
In line with the appreciating peso, the Central Bank trended down its bid rate for the dollar, starting at 26.235 to 26.23 pesos, traders said. However, it did not buy or sell dollars.
